# zokor API (generated by docs/gen_api.sh from zokor/; do not edit)
#
# `import "zokor";` then `zokor.<name>`. Methods are `value.name(..)`;
# `self` is omitted. Times are int nanoseconds, statuses i32.
# Recipes: docs/llms-small.txt.

## auth.sl -- Authentication helpers: bearer JWTs, Basic credentials and API keys.
gc struct JwtAuth { keys: [bytes], audience: str, issuer: str, leeway: int }
jwt_auth(secrets: [str]) -> result[JwtAuth, str]
    Secrets of at least 32 bytes each, newest first.
jwt_auth_from(cfg: Config) -> JwtAuth
    JWT_SECRETS (comma-separated, newest first), JWT_AUDIENCE, JWT_ISSUER and JWT_LEEWAY (seconds, default 30).
sign_token[T](claims: T, a: JwtAuth) -> result[str, str]
    A token for `claims`, signed with the newest key.
token_problem(token: str, a: JwtAuth, now: int) -> str
    Why `token` is not acceptable at `now`, or "" when it is.
bearer_claims[S, T](c: Ctx[S], a: JwtAuth) -> result[T, http.Response]
    The token's claims as your own type, once the token has passed every check; otherwise the 401 to send.
gc struct BasicCredentials { user: str, password: str }
basic_credentials[S](c: Ctx[S]) -> opt[BasicCredentials]
    The credentials of an `Authorization: Basic` header, or none when there is no such header or it does not decode to...
basic_matches(got: BasicCredentials, user: str, password: str) -> bool
    Whether `got` is `user` / `password`.
basic_denied[S](c: Ctx[S], realm: str) -> http.Response
    The 401 that asks a browser for Basic credentials for `realm`.
gc struct ApiKeys { names: [str], digests: [bytes] }
api_keys(entries: [str]) -> result[ApiKeys, str]
    `name:key` entries; each key at least 24 bytes.
api_keys_from(cfg: Config) -> ApiKeys
    API_KEYS: comma-separated `name:key` entries.
api_key_client[S](c: Ctx[S], keys: ApiKeys) -> opt[str]
    The name of the client whose key is in the X-Api-Key header, or none.

no_trusted_proxies() -> TrustedProxies

    "a.b.c.d" as an unsigned 32-bit value, or -1.

TrustedProxies.is_empty() -> bool

client_ip_of(peer_ip: str, headers: bytes, tp: TrustedProxies) -> str
    Who the request came from.

## conditional.sl -- Conditional requests (RFC 9110 section 13): answer "not modified" when the client already has the current version, and refuse...
etag_of(data: bytes) -> str
    A strong entity tag for `data`: its length and 64-bit FNV-1a hash, quoted.
with_validators(resp: http.Response, etag: str, last_modified: opt[timez.Time]) -> http.Response
    `resp` with ETag (when `etag` is not "") and Last-Modified (when known, to the second: an HTTP date has no fraction).
not_modified(etag: str, last_modified: opt[timez.Time]) -> http.Response
    The 304 for a read whose validators matched: no body, and the validators the 200 would have carried.
preconditions[S](c: Ctx[S], etag: str, last_modified: opt[timez.Time]) -> opt[http.Response]
    What a conditional request's headers decide, before the handler does its work: some(304) or some(412) to send as is, none to...

enum SameSite { LAX, STRICT, NONE }
gc struct Cookie { name: str, value: str, path: str, domain: str, max_age: int, expires: opt[timez.Time], secure: bool, http_only: bool, same_site: SameSite, partitioned: bool }

    The Set-Cookie value for `c`, unchecked: callers check first.
set_cookie(resp: http.Response, c: Cookie) -> result[http.Response, str]
    `resp` with a Set-Cookie header for `c`, or why `c` cannot be sent.
clear_cookie(resp: http.Response, name: str, path: str, domain: str) -> result[http.Response, str]
    Tells the browser to delete `name`.
parse_cookies(header: str) -> map[str]str
    Every well-formed name=value pair in a Cookie header, in order; a pair without `=`, with a bad name or with bytes a cookie...
gc struct CookieKeys { keys: [bytes] }
cookie_keys(keys: [str]) -> result[CookieKeys, str]
    Keys of at least 32 bytes each, newest first.
cookie_keys_from(cfg: Config) -> CookieKeys
    COOKIE_KEYS, comma-separated, newest first.
constant_time_equal(a: bytes, b: bytes) -> bool
    Compares in time that depends only on the lengths, so a forged signature cannot be found a byte at a time by timing the answer.
signed_cookie(name: str, value: str, keys: CookieKeys) -> result[Cookie, str]
    A cookie whose value is `value.signature`.
signed_value[S](c: Ctx[S], name: str, keys: CookieKeys) -> opt[str]
    The value of signed cookie `name` when its signature matches any key, none when it is missing, unsigned or forged.
verify_signed(name: str, raw: str, keys: CookieKeys) -> opt[str]

    Off: no origins.

    The defaults, for these origins.

    What is wrong with `p`, or "" when it is usable.

    CORS_ORIGINS (comma-separated), CORS_METHODS, CORS_HEADERS, CORS_EXPOSE (comma-separated, replacing the defaults),...
gc struct Cors { on: bool, any: bool, credentials: bool, origins: [str], allow_methods: str, allow_headers: str, allow_headers_lower: [str], expose: str, max_age: str }
    What the router keeps: the policy, and the header values built once.

Cors.allows(origin: str) -> bool
    Whether `origin` (an Origin header's value) is allowed.
Cors.apply(resp: http.Response, origin: str) -> http.Response
    The headers for an ordinary response to a request with this Origin ("" when it had none).
Cors.preflight(origin: str) -> http.Response
    The answer to a preflight from `origin`.
is_preflight(method: str, raw_headers: bytes) -> bool
    Whether a request is a CORS preflight: OPTIONS, with an Origin and the method the real request will use.

code_names(r: Registry) -> [str]

## jobs.sl -- Background jobs: work on a schedule, and work queued to run later.
gc struct JobCtx[S] { state: S, name: str, payload: str, attempt: int, due: timez.Time, deadline: until }
    What a run gets: the service's state, which run this is, and the deadline to pass to everything that can block.
gc struct Jobs[S] { state: S, zone: timez.Zone, clock: timez.Clock, logger: Logger, default_timeout: int, scheduled: [ScheduledJob[S]], kinds: [JobKind[S]], queue: [QueuedJob], lock: mutex, in_flight: int, stopping: bool, failures: int }
new_jobs[S](state: S) -> Jobs[S]
job_backoff(attempt: int) -> int
    The wait before try `attempt + 1`: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ...
Jobs.every(name: str, spec: str, run: fn(JobCtx[S]) -> result[int, str], timeout: int) -> result[int, str]
    Runs `run` on the cron schedule `spec` (see timez.parse_cron), each run given `timeout` nanoseconds as its deadline.
Jobs.handle(kind: str, run: fn(JobCtx[S]) -> result[int, str], attempts: int) -> result[int, str]
    Registers what runs a queued job of `kind`, and how many tries it gets (at least 1).
Jobs.enqueue(kind: str, payload: str, at: timez.Time) -> result[int, str]
    Queues one run of `kind` with `payload`, due at `at` (now or in the past runs at the next tick).
Jobs.queued() -> int
    Queued runs not yet started.
Jobs.running() -> int
    Runs started and not yet finished.
Jobs.tick(now: timez.Time) -> int
    Starts every run due at `now` -- scheduled turns and queued jobs -- each in its own task, and returns how many it started.
Jobs.start() -> int
    Starts the scheduler: a task that ticks at each due time, and at least every quarter second so a stop or SIGTERM is seen quickly.
Jobs.stop() -> int
    Stops starting runs.
Jobs.wait_runs(timeout: int) -> bool
    Waits until no run is in progress, or `timeout` nanoseconds pass; true when none is.

## pagination.sl -- Pagination: offset pages and keyset (cursor) pages, one envelope for both, so a client reads every list the same way:
struct Page { limit: int, offset: int, cursor: str, by_cursor: bool }
    What the request asked for, checked.
Page.fetch() -> int
    How many rows to ask the database for: one more than the page, so the response knows whether there is a next page without a count.
page_of[S](c: Ctx[S], default_limit: int, max_limit: int) -> result[Page, http.Response]
    The page `c` asks for: `limit` (default `default_limit`, at most `max_limit`), and either `offset` or `cursor`.
encode_cursor(parts: [str]) -> str
    The opaque cursor for a row whose sort key is `parts`.
decode_cursor(cursor: str) -> result[[str], str]
    The key parts of a cursor, err when it is not one encode_cursor made.
cursor_parts(p: Page) -> [str]
    The key parts of the cursor `p` came with ([] on the first page).
offset_page[S, T](c: Ctx[S], p: Page, rows: [T], total: opt[int]) -> http.Response
    An offset page of `rows` -- up to p.fetch() of them; one past the limit means there is a next page -- in the envelope, with Link.

pong_frame(payload: bytes) -> bytes

close_because(c: Conn, why: str) -> bytes
    The close a protocol error calls for: 1002, with the reason, and the connection marked shut so nothing else is sent.
gc struct SioSettings { ping_interval_ms: int, ping_timeout_ms: int, max_payload: int }
default_sio() -> SioSettings
enum SioKind { Open, Connect, Event, Ack, Ping, Disconnect, Other }
gc struct SioEvent { kind: SioKind, namespace: str, name: str, args_json: str, ack: int }
sio_open(c: Conn, sid: str, s: SioSettings) -> bytes
    The first thing a socket.io connection needs: its session id and the keepalive timings, as a text frame.
sio_receive(c: Conn, m: Message) -> result[SioEvent, str]
    Turns one WebSocket text message into a socket.io event.

    The answer to a CONNECT.
sio_connect_error(namespace: str, why: str) -> bytes

    `emit(name, args)`.

    The reply to an event that carried an ack id.

## internal/multipart (reached as UploadRules.limits)
